**The key move is Ne3+** - a devastating knight fork!

The knight gives check to the King on f5 while simultaneously attacking the undefended Rook on d1. After the King moves (Kg4, Ke5, Ke4, or Kg6—all forced), Black plays Nxd1, winning the Rook. White can recapture with Rxd1, but Black has won the exchange (Rook for Knight), a decisive material advantage.

This is a classic pattern: look for ways your pieces can do multiple jobs at once. The fork is one of the most powerful tactical themes in chess.
